text:
jia: Seeing a sharp uptick in Xid 79 on us-west1 A10 pools since ~20:10 UTC. Embedding hotpath looks correlated. Anyone seeing this?

rohit: Confirming. Alerting showed 42 Xid79 in the last 10m on rack r12. Majority on nodes r12-host7/gpu0 and r12-host9/gpu2.

infra-bot: Alert: XID 79 spike on cluster us-west1-prod-a10 (count=42, window=10m). Linked ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-3287

sarah: Can you paste a sample dmesg/pcie log from one of the affected hosts?

jia: here's a trimmed dmesg sample from r12-host7:```
[Aug 12 20:08:11] NVRM: Xid (79) a: 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000
[Aug 12 20:08:11] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3b:00.0: GPU panic: RECOVERED (pcie timeout?)
[Aug 12 20:08:12] kernel: pciehp 0000:3b:00.0:pciehp: Slot #0: Link down
[Aug 12 20:08:12] kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
```

rohit: Looks like PCIe recoveries plus ECC corrected counts rising. Can you run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `lspci -vvv` on the hosts and paste? Also grab `dmesg | grep -i pcie`

jia: ran ECC query on r12-host7:```
GPU 0 ECC errors (Corrected): 128
GPU 0 ECC errors (Uncorrected): 0
GPU 1 ECC errors (Corrected): 2
```Logs uploaded to OPS-3287.

ana: (joined) Which route is this coming from? embedder or decode?

jia: embedding service (embedder-v2) – small prompt sizes but very high QPS. Batching disabled on that path; most requests are single-example micro-requests.

tom: Hypothesis: sustained small-batch high-frequency IO is stressing PCIe fabric on these slots, causing recoveries -> Xid79. We saw a similar pattern last month after the kernel bump.

rohit: We rolled kernel 5.15.0-xyz on us-west1 two days ago. Could be a regression in PCIe driver path. Worth checking kernel logs across updated hosts.

sarah: Proposed action: soft-drain the most affected hosts, divert embed traffic to us-east1 as a temporary mitigation, run vendor diagnostics on flagged cards, and collect full PCIe + ECC counters. If ECC uncorrected increases, schedule RMA.

jia: starting soft drain on r12-host7 now: `./clusterctl drain-host r12-host7 --reason 'xid79-triage' --soft`

infra-bot: Traffic reroute initiated: 250 qps of embed traffic moved to us-east1-embedders. ETA ~2m.

ana: Cost flag: moving traffic to us-east1 will bump daily costs ~+$3k/day at current load due to instance mix and egress. Approve?

sarah: :thumbsup: Approve for up to 24h while we triage.

tom: For triage we should collect `nvidia-smi dmon` traces and use `setpci` to dump AER counters. I'll run remote diagnostics on r12-host7 and r12-host9.

rohit: Also verify if recent image/quantization changes increased memory/PCIe bandwidth (embedder-v2:sha@a1b2c3d rolled 3 days ago). If so, rollback on a small % of workers to compare.

jia: rolling back embedder image on 10% canary now to see if Xid rate changes.

sarah: If PCIe fabric is flaky we'll need vendor RMA. Ana, can you open the vendor ticket and reserve spare A10s?

ana: Filing RMA + spare allocation. Expect vendor SLA 3-5 business days. We'll reuse hot spares for hotfixes.

jia: Marking r12-host7 for replacement if corrected ECC increases >200 in next 24h. Maintenance mode set.

tom: Also pushing a temporary batching middleware on the embed route to aggregate single-item requests into micro-batches (target batch size 8, latency SLO soft cap). I'll push canary in 10m.

rohit: Long-term item: enable prefix/KV caching and default batching on embedder routes to reduce per-token PCIe churn. Add to Optimize backlog.

sarah: Owners: jia (soft drains + logs), tom (canary batching + diag), rohit (kernel/pcie investigation), ana (RMA + cost). I'll track the ticket and follow up.

infra-bot: OPS-3287 updated: owners assigned, next automated update in 2h.

jia: Update: soft drain completed on r12-host7, sessions gracefully drained, logs uploaded to OPS-3287 (dmesg, lspci, nvidia-smi traces).

tom: dmon traces running now, will attach to ticket when complete. Initial look: bursts line up with Xid spikes.

sarah: Thanks team. Reconvene here in 60m for status update. :coffee:
